title: Paseo SLP — how a brief becomes a controlled operation

basis.note: Explanatory animation of the working source. Not footage of a live daemon and not E2E proof.

scenes.title: How a brief becomes a controlled operation

cues.text: Paseo SLP organizes coding agents as a Supervisor, a Lead, and independent Peers.
Here's how a brief becomes a controlled operation, and where human judgment still matters.
Three owners share the work.
Paseo runs sessions, workspaces and agent parentage.
The plugin adds role policy, and a runtime that checks recorded facts.
The Human keeps intent, authority and final acceptance.
And the plugin is not an agent scheduler.

scenes.title: Role policy is read. Enforcement is checked.

cues.text: Role policy is what a seat reads, layered from common rules down to one assignment.
Lower layers narrow, never widen.
Enforcement is code, checking membership, ownership and revisions on guarded desk calls.
Policy guides judgment. Enforcement guards recorded facts.

scenes.title: A checkout, a published runtime and a session are different objects

cues.text: The SLP Manager activates a published runtime.
Verified bytes land in a pinned runtime directory, with launchers and profiles.
A binding pins the runtime, Node, transport and daemon home.
At launch, a hook or wrapper delivers the role before the provider starts.
Rebinding changes future launches; running sessions keep their bytes.

scenes.title: A title is presentation. Membership is identity.

cues.text: A session acts on the desk only through bound membership.
It records the exact agent, runtime family, role, directory and binding generation.
Every desk call crosses the bridge: fresh identity, capability, strict schema.
The desk is an append-only, hash-chained ledger, shared by related worktrees.
It guards desk calls. It is not a shell sandbox.

scenes.title: One writer per scope. Review selected, then pinned.

cues.text: Each moving scope has one writer.
Review is selected: required, not required, or exempt with an authority pointer.
A review round pins the candidate, scope, brief and neutral mandate.
Change one, and the review goes stale.
Owner and writer can't clear their own independent gate.

scenes.title: The worker receives work only after binding

cues.text: Managed dispatch is a chain of recorded steps.
Reserve the attempt, then create the worker with no work prompt.
Verify its observed runtime, labels, parent, workspace and directory.
Bind the membership, claim the scope, and only then send the work.
Late registration returns seat-pending and sends nothing.
A lost create receipt stays uncertain, and is never blindly replaced.

scenes.title: A finished prerequisite is not necessarily usable

cues.text: A finished prerequisite isn't automatically usable.
Readiness needs a qualified result, and availability measured in the consumer's actual base.
B and C are landed and qualified, but D's base has only B. So D stays blocked.
Reopening A invalidates readiness; history keeps what was consumed.

scenes.title: One issued effect, recorded on both sides of the cut

cues.text: A ledger transaction can't make a host effect atomic.
So each effect is split: intent, locked issue, the bounded SDK or Git call, then observe.
Lose the receipt, and the effect stays uncertain.
Exact replay returns the recorded outcome; reconciliation measures the original identity.
A fresh request is not recovery. There's no automatic retry engine.

scenes.title: Integrate a delta, preserve unrelated work

cues.text: Integration measures the worker's base, its result, and the actual target.
A three-way merge keeps unrelated work, and holds conflicts.
Stage builds the candidate outside the target; check runs owner-pinned recipes.
Land rechecks, records a recovery plan, backs up, applies, and measures.
It never commits, pushes, or deploys.

scenes.title: Cleanup is a proof-gated workflow too

cues.text: Cleanup is gated by proof, too.
First, an account binds the original proof and the resource inventory.
The stage is removed under its own permit, and only then the backup.
Each gets two total cycles. Exhaustion keeps the obligation, instead of looping.

scenes.title: What the mechanism does not prove

cues.text: Some limits stay explicit.
Stop fences new effects, but doesn't prove a running turn was cancelled.
Archive doesn't prove processes are quiescent.
A grant reference doesn't authenticate a Human grant.
Language guidance, quota fallback, Jev routing and supervision are opt-in, not an autonomous scheduler.

scenes.title: Durable, inspectable work — with real human judgment

cues.text: Work, ownership, review and effects survive interruption, and stay inspectable in Read SLP work.
Human judgment and project acceptance remain real decisions.
For details and source pins, open docs/plugin-explained.html.
